commits.pr_title: [1/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Refactor DSV4 KV cache config construction
commits.pr_body:
PR #42374 (first part of RFC #42082) has been split into 4 PRs:

-> #44454 [1/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Refactor DSV4 KV cache config
#44455 [2/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Pack K/V into the content dim across attention backends
#44456 [3/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Standardize Mamba cache; drop `get_transfer_cache_regions`
#44458 [4/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Standardize KV cache layout


## Summary

Extracts the per-page-size layer bucketing logic out of `_get_kv_cache_config_deepseek_v4` into a reusable helper, `_bucket_layers_by_page_size`. Behavior-preserving: same allocation pattern (one `KVCacheTensor` per `(slot_idx, page_size)`), same `shared_by` semantics.

## Changes

- Add `_bucket_layers_by_page_size(kv_cache_groups)` handling both `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` (per-layer page sizes) and regular specs.
- Rewrite `_get_kv_cache_config_deepseek_v4()` to use it.
- Simplify the DSV4 branch of `_pool_bytes_per_block()` to use bucket-derived values.

## Test Results (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=4xB200, fp8 KV cache)

  - KV cache: 333,437 tokens (+1.16% vs main's 329,601) — previous code over-counted per-block cost when slot counts differ across page sizes
  - GSM8K: 97.0% accuracy (5-shot, 200q, temp=0)

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude).

Updated torch version when requesting `xpu`. As per the [official documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.12/notes/get_start_xpu.html), the way to install xpu versions is:

```sh
pip3 install torch==2.11.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu
```

Installing with `+xpu` leads to this error:

```
 No solution found when resolving dependencies for split (markers: python_full_version >= '3.12'):
  ╰─▶ Because there is no version of torch==2.11.0+xpu and your project depends on torch==2.11.0+xpu, we can conclude that your project's requirements are
      unsatisfiable.
```

commits.pr_title: [CI] Stabilize the multi-audio OpenAI server path
commits.pr_body:
This PR stabilizes the multi-audio OpenAI server path when a chat request exceeds `--limit-mm-per-prompt audio=2`. The failing test intentionally sends too many audio inputs, expects a 400 `BadRequestError`, and then immediately checks that the same server still accepts a follow-up `/v1/completions` request:

```text
tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_audio.py::test_multi_audio_input[audio_urls1-fixie-ai/ultravox-v0_5-llama-3_2-1b]
```

The over-limit request was already logically a client validation failure, but it was raised as a plain `ValueError` after Pydantic request parsing. In the observed flaky runs, the response could still be a 400 while the server logged an ASGI application exception and the client-side health probe sometimes saw:

```text
httpx.ReadError
openai.APIConnectionError: Connection error.
```

The fix therefore needs to do two things:
- make multimodal item-limit violations first-class vLLM validation errors at the OpenAI API boundary;
- avoid creating async media coroutines during chat parsing until the request has passed parse-time item-limit validation.

The small internal split of `BaseMultiModalItemTracker.add()` into `add()` and `_validate_add()` supports that second point. `_validate_add()` is private; it does not add a new public tracker API. Also, async parsers now store values like:

```python
partial(self._audio_with_uuid_async, audio_url, uuid)
```

instead of:

```python
self._audio_with_uuid_async(audio_url, uuid)
```

This is necessary because calling an async function creates a coroutine object immediately. If parsing later rejects the request before `resolve_items()` is reached, that coroutine can be left unawaited. Deferring coroutine creation until `resolve_items()` is preferable to eager coroutine creation plus cleanup because it removes the failure-mode entirely instead of adding another recovery path.

cc @kenroche

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Fix multimodal torch.compile troubleshooting to not use removed VLLM_TORCH_COMPILE_LEVEL
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The "Compilation Errors" troubleshooting section in `docs/design/torch_compile_multimodal.md` tells users to disable compilation like this:

```bash
VLLM_TORCH_COMPILE_LEVEL=0 vllm serve <model> --compilation-config='{"compile_mm_encoder":"false"}'
```

`VLLM_TORCH_COMPILE_LEVEL` no longer exists anywhere in the codebase — torch.compile control was moved to `CompilationConfig` / the `-O` optimization levels. The env var is silently ignored, so following this step does **not** actually disable compilation: the model still runs compiled, defeating the "verify the model works without compilation" instruction.

## Change

Use the documented way to turn off torch.compile + CUDA graphs:

```bash
vllm serve <model> --enforce-eager --compilation-config='{"compile_mm_encoder":"false"}'
```

Per `docs/design/debug_vllm_compile.md`, `--enforce-eager` (→ `enforce_eager=True`) is "Turn off torch.compile and CUDAGraphs". I kept the explicit `compile_mm_encoder: false` to preserve the original intent of also skipping the MM encoder.

One-line doc change.

## Not a duplicate

Per `AGENTS.md` duplicate-work checks (on `main` @ `53b88d1d`):

```
grep -rn VLLM_TORCH_COMPILE_LEVEL docs/ vllm/   # only the doc line above; no code definition
gh issue list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search "VLLM_TORCH_COMPILE_LEVEL"  # nothing about this doc
gh pr list    --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search "VLLM_TORCH_COMPILE_LEVEL"  # none
```

The only open PR touching `torch_compile_multimodal.md` historically is #30549 (WhisperEncoder), which does not modify this troubleshooting section.

## Test plan

```bash
# Confirm the env var is dead (no consumers anywhere):
grep -rn "VLLM_TORCH_COMPILE_LEVEL" . --include='*.py'   # (excluding the doc) -> no matches

pre-commit run --files docs/design/torch_compile_multimodal.md
```

`typos`, `markdownlint-cli2`, and the other applicable hooks pass on the changed file. (`update-dockerfile-graph` errors with `Executable /bin/bash not found` — a Windows-host limitation unrelated to this doc; it runs on Linux CI.)

---

AI-assisted (Claude Code); reviewed end-to-end by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Fix per-group block_size/block_hash and group_idx in MooncakeStoreConnector KV events
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`MooncakeStoreConnector` emits `BlockStored` KV events so external subscribers can track which KV blocks are present in the store. In hybrid / multi-group (HMA) configurations — and whenever a group's `block_size` is larger than the connector's `hash_block_size` — three fields of the emitted event were wrong.

1. **`block_hashes`** used `req_meta.block_hashes[chunk_idx]`, which indexes the request's *hash-granular* hash list with a *chunk* index. When `block_size > hash_block_size`, consecutive hashes are merged into one chunk hash via `BlockHashListWithBlockSize`, so this picked the wrong hash and the event advertised a `block_hash` that does not match the key the block is actually stored under. A consumer indexing the store by that hash would miss or mismatch. The fix derives the hash directly from the store key being written (`BlockHash(bytes.fromhex(key.chunk_hash))`), so the event hash and the storage key agree by construction. For the uniform single-group case (`block_size == hash_block_size`) this is identical to the previous behavior, so nothing regresses there.

2. **`block_size`** used a single global `original_block_size` (`cache_config.block_size`), which is wrong for groups whose block size differs. It now uses the per-group `db.block_size`.

3. **`group_idx`** was not set, so multi-group consumers could not attribute an event to its KV-cache group. It is now populated from the per-group loop index. `BlockStored.group_idx` already exists, so no event-schema change is needed.

With `original_block_size` no longer read anywhere after (2), the now-dead field and its plumbing (scheduler attribute, `ReqMeta` field/parameter, worker attribute, and test references) are removed. This mechanical cleanup is bundled with the substantive fix rather than shipped on its own.

## Test

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py -q
# 66 passed

pre-commit run ruff-check --files <changed files>
# Passed
```

The worker tests include a case with `enable_kv_event=True` and a `block_size > hash_block_size` ("double hash") group, which exercises the corrected event fields.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs on vllm-project/vllm (`mooncake kv event`, `MooncakeStoreConnector`, `mooncake BlockStored`). The nearby open mooncake PRs are unrelated in scope: #43742 (release GPU pin on failed store), #43701 (DummyClient mode), #42199 (DP worker bootstrap timeout). None touch `BlockStored` per-group correctness.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The author has reviewed every changed line and run the tests listed above.

commits.pr_title: [feature] add index share feature for DSA MTP
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR implements IndexCache top-k index reuse for DeepSeek Sparse MLA's MTP Layer, inspired by [IndexCache: Accelerating Sparse Attention via Cross-Layer Index Reuse](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.12201).

The core idea is to avoid running the sparse attention indexer in every layer or every MTP speculative step when the top-k token selections can be reused. The implementation adds support for carrying `topk_indices` through the DeepSeek MLA/MTP forward path and reusing the existing `topk_indices_buffer` when `skip_topk` is enabled.

For MTP, this PR introduces the `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` behavior:

- When `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=True`, the first draft token computes its own `topk_indices`, while subsequent draft proposals reuse the `topk_indices_buffer`.
- When `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=False`, each draft proposal computes its own `topk_indices` independently.
## What changed

- Pass `topk_indices` through DeepSeek MLA attention, decoder layers, and MTP layers.
- Mark MTP layers as index-reuse consumers so they skip redundant top-k recomputation.
- Let MTP compute its own top-k indices on step 0, then reuse them for later speculative steps.
- Remove target/draft `topk_indices_buffer` sharing; the draft model now owns and reuses its own buffer.
- Add support for `index_topk_freq`, `index_topk_pattern`, and `index_skip_topk_offset` to configure which layers run the indexer.
- Fix `qk_rope_head_dim` loading for affected MLA configs by reading the raw `config.json` value when the transformers attribute mapping is corrupted.

commits.pr_title: [DSV4] Decouple DS V4 Sparse MLA Metadata from DS V3.2
[ROCm][MLA] Replace torch.cat in sparse-MLA forward_mqa with fused concat_mla_q
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

In the ROCm sparse-MLA backend, `forward_mqa` builds `q = torch.cat([ql_nope, q_pe], dim=-1)` once per layer per forward pass. On DeepSeek-V3.2 (61 sparse-MLA layers on the decode path) this adds up to **61 fresh tensor allocations and 61 `aten::CatArrayBatchedCopy` kernel launches per decode step**, ≈ 360 µs at MC=4 (≈ 4% of a decode step measured at TP=4, ISL=1000, OSL=100 on MI355X).

The fused `ops.concat_mla_q(ql_nope, q_pe, q_out)` already exists in `vllm/_custom_ops.py` and is already used by `FlashMLASparseImpl.forward_mqa` at `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py:1028`. This PR plugs it into `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` against a preallocated workspace buffer sized `(max_num_batched_tokens, num_heads, head_size)`, so:

- No per-layer allocation on the decode hot path.
- Output address is stable across CUDA graph capture/replay (same pattern `FlashMLASparseImpl` uses today).
- One fused kernel instead of one ATen cat.

The patch is numerically identical to the `torch.cat` it replaces (no change in GSM8K, see below).

The workspace buffer is allocated using `vllm_config.model_config.dtype` so both bf16 and fp16 paths advertised by `ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend.supported_dtypes` get matching-dtype storage (per @gemini-code-assist review).

## Performance

Setup: DeepSeek-V3.2 (sparse-FP8) on 4× MI355X, TP=4, MC=4, ISL=1000, OSL=100, 32 prompts per run, 4 runs per build (seeds 42/42/7/13), deterministic integer-prompt feed.

Build matrix (everything is the published nightly image except the file in this PR):

- **Baseline**: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-32b7177909d1c9928bcedd81de7de5a1fa21d2b3` (upstream `0.21.1rc1.dev28+g32b717790`, file `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` matches `main` at the time of writing).
- **main + this PR**: same image, with this PR's `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` bind-mounted on top.

Both builds run with the AITER `module_custom_all_reduce.so` from the upcoming AITER v0.14 (pinned to ROCm/aiter@`c71075ced`, "Fix 2-stage fused_allreduce_rmsnorm memory ordering", #2890) bind-mounted on top of the image's AITER 0.13. This is unrelated to the change in this PR — it is needed to keep the GSM8K accuracy comparison meaningful and is symmetric across baseline and patched (so it cannot account for the delta below).

| Build | Mean TPOT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | P99 TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline (n=4) | 17.54 | 17.08 | 21.45 | 183.5 |
| **main + this PR** (n=4) | **17.09** | **16.92** | **18.57** | **194.1** |
| delta | **-0.46 ms (-2.6%)** | **-0.16 ms (-0.9%)** | **-2.88 ms (-13.4%)** | **+5.8%** |

Run-to-run noise on a single node is ≈ ±0.4 ms mean TPOT; the patched run is below the baseline range for every seed. The P99 improvement is the strongest signal — eliminating the per-layer ATen allocation removes a recurring tail-latency contributor.

Server:

```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

Bench:

```
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1000 --random-output-len 100 \
  --random-prompt-as-token-ids \
  --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 4 \
  --ignore-eos --seed {42,7,13}
```

## Accuracy

GSM8K, n=200, num_fewshot=5, `--gen_kwargs temperature=0,seed=42` (greedy), evaluated against the raw `/v1/completions` endpoint (matches `.buildkite/lm-eval-harness/run-lm-eval-gsm-vllm-baseline.sh`), `transformers==4.57.1`.

| Build | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0.945 ± 0.016 | 0.945 ± 0.016 |
| main + this PR | 0.945 ± 0.016 | 0.945 ± 0.016 |

Identical accuracy; expected, since the patch is numerically identical to the existing `torch.cat`.

## Single-prompt sanity (patched server, greedy)

Spot-checks against `/v1/chat/completions` with `temperature=0`:

| Prompt | Output |
|---|---|
| `What is 17 times 23? Return only the integer.` | `\( 17 \times 23 = 391 \)` |
| `What is the capital of France? Answer with the city name only.` | `Paris` |
| `What is the largest planet in our solar system? Reply with one word.` | `Jupiter` |
| `A train leaves at 3:00 PM and arrives 2.5 hours later. What time does it arrive in HH:MM 24-hour format? Reply with just HH:MM.` | `17:30` |

All four expected answers; no spurious continuations, no language drift.

## Static checks

- `python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 1 "3.10"` — clean
- mypy for Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 (full CI matrix) — clean
- `ruff check vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` — All checks passed
- `ruff format --check vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` — already formatted

## Cross-reference

Mirrors the workspace-buffer + `ops.concat_mla_q` pattern that `FlashMLASparseImpl.forward_mqa` already uses at `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py:1028`.

cc @tjtanaa

commits.pr_title: [BugFix] Resolve multiple async kv load deadlock
commits.pr_body:
This is a different fix for the issue targeted by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40968.

The changes are simpler and the resulting behavior should also be better - we avoid async-loading new kv if it would occupy blocks required for other in-flight chunked prefills or async-loading requests.

Note: we apply this throttle to async kv loads only, rather than chunked-prefill requests in general, since the latter are naturally throttled by batch capacity and are also already eligible for preemption.

cc @Dao007forever

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Fused MoE W4A16 HIP kernel for AMD RDNA3 (gfx1100)
commits.pr_body:
### Summary

Native HIP kernel for W4A16 MoE on RDNA3 (gfx1100), replacing the Triton
`fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` path. It uses the same dequant + dot primitives as
the dense W4A16 kernel: `v_dot2_f32_f16` / `v_dot2_f32_bf16`, exllama bit-trick
dequant, and 64-bit CAS atomic output.

### What it does

- **Fused HIP kernel** (`csrc/rocm/moe_q_gemm_rdna3.cu`): expert routing + W4A16
  GEMM in a single kernel launch. Templated on `BLOCK_SIZE_M = {1, 2, 4, 8}`.
  The bf16 `M=1` fast path skips LDS staging (direct global read, with a
  `v_dot2_f32_bf16` opacity trick to defeat InstCombine).
- **`output_topk` parameter**: fuses `moe_sum` into the w2 kernel — writes
  directly to `out[token_id / top_k]` via atomics, eliminating a separate kernel
  launch and the intermediate buffer.
- **Decode optimizations**: `BLOCK_SIZE_M = 1` for small `M` (eliminates ~75% of
  padding waste); pre-allocated w1/act buffers (eliminates per-layer
  `torch.zeros`).
- **Extensible dispatch** (`_try_get_rocm_moe_method()`): checks architecture and
  op availability in priority order. New architectures (RDNA4, CDNA) can be added
  as branches. Falls through to Triton WNA16 if no native kernel is available.
- **Build guards**: the `.cu` is only compiled when `VLLM_GPU_ARCHES` contains
  `gfx1100`; the torch op is registered under `#ifdef VLLM_ROCM_GFX1100`; the
  Python side checks `hasattr(torch.ops._rocm_C, "moe_gptq_gemm_rdna3")`.

Measured on 1× RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) via EvalScope `perf`, `openqa` dataset,
